Note::strip_zero_width¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::strip_zero_width() const

Remove Invisible Zero-Width Characters From Every Cell¶

strip_zero_width() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with zero-width characters removed from anywhere in each cell: the zero-width space (U+200B), zero-width non-joiner (U+200C), zero-width joiner (U+200D), the word joiner (U+2060), and the zero-width no-break space / BOM (U+FEFF).

These characters render as nothing but still count as bytes, so they defeat exact-match lookups, inflate length checks, and can be used to smuggle markers through text. Stripping them normalises a cell to what a reader actually sees.

strip_zero_width removes the characters wherever they appear — unlike strip_bom, which only removes a U+FEFF at the very start. It is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: A Batch¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note(
    {std::string("a") + "\xE2\x80\x8B" + "b" + "\xEF\xBB\xBF" + "c", "clean"})
    .strip_zero_width();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["abc", "clean"]

The zero-width space between a and b and the U+FEFF between b and c are both removed.

  • Note::strip_bom: remove only a leading U+FEFF.

  • Note::remove_control_chars: remove ASCII control bytes.
